AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a solid fundamental case with strong trajectory, but valuation at the top of its recent range tempers enthusiasm. Pillar 1 (Fundamentals): AWS is reaccelerating to 28% YoY growth on a $150B run rate with a $364B backlog, driving record 13.1% operating margins in Q1 2026. Revenue grew 17% YoY to $181.5B, and EPS of $2.78 crushed consensus of $1.63. Quarterly trajectory shows accelerating revenue ($155.7B→$167.7B→$180.2B) and EPS ($1.59→$1.68→$1.95) over three quarters. 2025. Balance sheet equity grew to33%.B to $.37BBBQ $369.6BB debt-to equity is0.15 is manageable. Custom silicon business (~$20B annually growing triple-digit growth. However, massive $200B capex front-loaded is press to FCF pressure from $25.B to $1.2B. Pillar 2 (Valuation): P/E of38.9 is the P/B 8.0, p_s 4.3x are at the top of the 3-month range (pe iluted 28.2-39.0, p_b 5.8-8.3). The stock has rallied 31.8% in one quarter, pricing in much of the positive AWS narrative. At current levels, the market is paying peak multiples for the same earnings power that was available at 28-29x P/E in Feb-Mar 2026. Pillar 3 (Catalyst): Q2 2026 guidance of $194-199B revenue is above consensus, and the Snowflake $6B AWS deal signals continued enterprise AI demand. However, the $200B capex plan creates near-term FCF pressure (trailing FCF collapsed 95% to $1.2B), and rising 10-year yields (4.45%) and oil ($92.65) add macro headwinds. The catalyst is modestly positive but not transformative enough to push beyond the +0.3-0.4 range.
